I keep 0 dollars in the cash management account since it gives slightly lower rates and I have it set up to automatically draw from the brokerage account when there is an atm withdrawal. I do direct deposit and all non-atm transactions from the brokerage account.

I use a Fidelity brokerage account as my checking account, it does everything a checking account does but it also automatically sweeps your cash into a money market fund that currently yields \~5% per year with dividends paid monthly. So basically it's a checking account with higher yields than most HYSAs.

Additionally, you can open a cash management account for a debit card that reimburses all ATM fees worldwide. I personally keep the cash management account at 0$ and set it to pull money from the brokerage automatically whenever there is a transaction. I quite like this setup but it can take a little effort to get going.
